title: Short-Circuit Logical Assignment Overload (The One-Line Conditional)
pattern: Combining optional unpacking, state assertion, and action execution into a single, compound short-circuiting logical expression.
why_bad: It creates a "mental speed bump." Combining side-effects with boolean assertions on a single line makes tracing through the code extremely difficult and obscures the exact point of failure during debugging.
detection: A single conditional block containing sequential, dependent logical operators (`&&` or `||`) where the left-hand expression is a prerequisite (e.g., `is_some()`) for the right-hand side's unwrapping or mutation.
counterexample: Simple, safe pointer validations or null checks like `if ptr.is_null() || unsafe { (*ptr).is_expired() }`. `Context-dependent`.
source: *The Art of Readable Code*, Chapter 7, "Beware of 'clever' nuggets of code" (p. 86-87).
